newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecom rejects partner plan.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecom rejects partner plan.

text.p: Portugal Telecom said on Thursday that it was seeking an international alliance but that it was not interested in any future partner taking a significant stake.
The company, which has been 49 percent privatised, had previously said that it was casting around for a strategic partner who could conceivably take a significant holding in the company.

"What would normally be called a strategic partner, that is somebody who would buy more than 20 percent...and have a significant say in the management, has been put aside," a spokeswoman told Reuters.

Earlier, the company issued a statement outlining its strategic objectives and saying that it would be looking for a "strategic alignment" that could involve the buying of just a symbolic stake in Portugal Telecom.
Analysts said that Telecom shares could fall on the Lisbon bourse on Friday in a knee-jerk reaction to the announcement.

Portugal Telecom has been one of the strongest performers on the bourse this year and the idea that a large foreign player was about to buy a significant chunk of stock could have been a factor in the strength of the share, they said.
"The first psychological reaction could be a fall, but then it would be a good opportunity to buy," said Jose Carlos Tomas of Banco Portugues de Investimento.
The spokeswoman said that a "symbolic" stake could be up to five percent.
